To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the introduction of a prospective payment system based on DRGs increases the number of secondary diagnosis in health care administrative registers.
the introduction of DRG based management systems in Swedish hospitals increased the number of recorded secondary diagnoses.
the introduction of DRG systems, irrespective of their use, focuses on diagnoses and increases the number of recorded diagnoses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the introduction of DRG systems on the number of secondary diagnosis in the Swedish national Hospital Discharge Register.
the impact of DRG-based payment systems on the number of secondary diagnosed conditions in administrative data.
the impact of DRG-based management on the recording of diagnoses in administrative data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increase of secondary diagnosis in the Swedish hospital care system is not a result of the introduction of prospective payment systems, but that the introduction of such a system increases the number of secondary diagnosis.
the introduction of DRG management systems has had an impact on the recording of diagnoses, but that other factors may also have contributed.
the introduction of a DRG-based prospective system increases the number of coded diagnoses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of DRG systems, in the early 199os, has influenced the number of coded diagnoses, and this has had an impact on the number of coded diagnosis per case.
the introduction of DRG systems, irrespective of the use of the system, increases the number of coded diagnoses.
the introduction of a DRG-based system increases the number of recorded secondary diagnoses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of DRG systems, irrespective of the use of the systems, increases the number of coded diagnoses.
DRG-based systems have an effect on the number of diagnoses recorded, which should be kept in mind when using administrative data.
the introduction of DRG systems, and other systems with a focus on diagnosis, may have contributed to the observed increase in the number secondary diagnoses.
